title: What is the cardinality of P(R)

problemStatement.plain: The power set of the real numbers has cardinality 2^𝔠 = 2^(2^ℵ₀) = ℶ₂, the second beth number. The aleph-index of ℶ₂ is independent of ZFC.
whyMatters: Exemplifies the beth hierarchy: ℶ₀ = ℵ₀ = |ℕ|, ℶ₁ = 𝔠 = |ℝ|, ℶ₂ = |𝒫(ℝ)|
Illustrates the ZFC independence of the Continuum Hypothesis and its consequences
König's theorem (cf(2^𝔠) > 𝔠) provides a genuine ZFC constraint on the aleph-index

open: What is the aleph-index of ℶ₂? (Independent of ZFC via Easton's theorem)
Is |𝒫(ℝ)| = ℵ₂? (Equivalent to GCH at the continuum level, ZFC-independent)

knowledge.progressSummary: Successfully formalized all ZFC-provable facts about |𝒫(ℝ)|: power set formula (= 2^𝔠), Cantor strict inequality, beth representation (= ℶ₂), and aleph lower bound (ℵ₁ < |𝒫(ℝ)|). Also proved conditional results under CH+GCH. Docker build passes with 0 sorries.
builtItems: cantors_theorem_oq01_summary: bundles all 4 key ZFC facts
insights: Lean4 ordinal arithmetic: omega does NOT work for Ordinal goals. Use rw [Order.succ_eq_add_one]; norm_num to prove (n : Ordinal) = Order.succ (n-1)
Cardinal.beth_succ requires the argument in Order.succ form — literal numeral 2 must be converted via Order.succ_eq_add_one
Cardinal.two_power_aleph0 : 2^ℵ₀ = 𝔠 closes the residual goal after unrolling beth_one
Universe pinning: all Cardinal statements need Cardinal.{0} annotation to avoid metavariable issues
Cardinal.mk_set and Cardinal.cantor are the primary Mathlib workhorses for this problem
mathlibGaps: König's theorem for cardinal products not directly accessible — axiomatized as konig_constraint_powerSet_real

approaches.name: Direct beth hierarchy unrolling
approaches.description: Use Cardinal.mk_set for |𝒫(ℝ)| = 2^#ℝ, Cardinal.mk_real for #ℝ = 𝔠, then unroll beth_succ to show ℶ₂ = 2^ℶ₁ = 2^𝔠
approaches.outcome: Compiles with 0 sorries. Key hurdle: ordinal literal conversion for beth_succ.
